label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: The empty classroom is recognizable through its partition, suspended ceiling with missing panels, right-wall whiteboard, rear fixtures and flag, and scattered floor debris.
The left partition, right whiteboard, rear fixtures, overhead ceiling damage, left-side debris and right-side yellow sheets retain the principal spatial relationships.
The whiteboard is substantially oversized vertically and reaches the ceiling, unlike the reference's board with a substantial wall band above it.
Light walls and ceiling, dark flooring and baseboards, gray debris, yellow sheets and the colored flag preserve the principal color organization. Shapes and surfaces are heavily simplified.
The interior and principal objects remain visible under broadly compatible soft illumination. Heavy grain and flatter lighting reduce quality without obscuring the main content.
Complementary viewpoints show consistent room depth, wall orientation, ceiling structure and volumetric debris, establishing a genuine three-dimensional scene.

Actual mesh objects provide separately addressable floor, walls, ceiling, board and debris geometry. Their finite meshes, parent chains and assigned materials are recorded, with valid shader connections.

dimension_scores.evidence: The distinctive room contents are recognizable, but oversized board geometry, simplified damage and altered framing weaken the match.
The enclosure and ceiling read coherently, and debris lies near the floor. Rigid stacked sheets and minimally represented fixture attachments reduce physical credibility.
The principal palette survives, but walls appear less warm, yellow sheets are pale, and damaged materials have overly regular rectangular silhouettes.
Severe visible render grain, uniformly clean surfaces, rigid flag geometry and block-like debris undermine realism.
The principal left-right and front-back arrangement is preserved, although the yellow sheets sit farther from the wall and the authored framing changes the room's apparent depth.
Most fixtures and debris have plausible relative sizes, but the whiteboard is too tall and the ceiling grid appears coarse.
Lighting keeps the room legible and provides contact shading, but grain and weak surface differentiation diminish the carpet, wall and debris materials.

Most major visible elements are present, including damaged ceiling sections, partition, whiteboard, flag, rear fixtures and debris. Ceiling light panels and finer damage details are not clearly reproduced.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
